So a later Gray bit change can show up before an earlier, delayed one. candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model follows the spec text literally: per-bit independence and restart on replacement (spec:653, AF-10.6.4-01; cell_sync.sv:89-93 comment and :158-169 code). The same spec requires that the flags are never optimistic and that the estimate differs only by in-flight updates, with the model on (spec:137-139, :517, :685, TEST-008 at :1246 "flags never optimistic", CC-10 at :979, rules.json:13573). Independent per-bit delays of up to 2 destination cycles can reorder Gray bit changes that are less than 2 destination cycles apart in the source. The synchronized pointer then decodes to a value the source never held, so the two spec statements cannot both hold. The pass/fail split matches exactly: every model-on run fails, while model_off.s1 and syn.s1 pass (results.json:37-50).
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform of w_rgray_s is available. The reordering mechanism is inferred from the RTL and from the failing value pattern (o_full_thr=1 with o_full=0 at threshold 8 is impossible for any valid pointer pair), not observed directly. small.s1 (DEPTH=2) passes this test, maybe only because a 2-bit pointer has fewer reorder chances in this short sequence.

candidates.evidence_for: The simulation model is a delivered part of the RTL (FEAT-009, spec:93) and it is what produces the bad synchronized values. Real synchronizers can only resolve a bit that changes close to the capture edge as old or new. An earlier Gray bit change, a full source period older, is stable, so real hardware never shows a later bit ahead of an earlier one. The model (cell_sync.sv:158-177) applies the extra delay to every change, whatever its timing, which is less realistic than the spec intends at :684 ("a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value"). The datapath RTL (wr.sv:106-126) is correct for coherent Gray inputs, and syn.s1 and model_off.s1 pass.
candidates.evidence_against: The model does exactly what spec 10.6.4 (AF-10.6.4-01, MUST) asks for. Changing it means changing a spec-mandated behavior, so the designer has to decide which statement wins. The full/occupancy logic in m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv shows no defect of its own.

candidates.evidence_for: The test leans on the model being Gray-coherent, which the spec does not state explicitly.
candidates.evidence_against: The check codes contract CHK-013(c) exactly (contract.json:524 vs test :212-214) and follows from REQ-FUNC-010 with the occupancy range 0..DEPTH. The independent SVA a_CHK_013 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:135-140) fails at the same time (NNC_FAIL CHK-013 @1681000). The stimulus is legal (static thresholds, no software reset, both resets released). The Python and the SVA agree, so the testbench is not the cause.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify the spec / fix the model (preferred): rewrite spec 10.6.4 so the metastability model keeps pointer coherence, then change m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-179 to match. Possible ways: (a) apply the extra delay only to a change that reaches the last stage within one destination cycle of the previous change of the same bus, or (b) model metastability as an old/new choice at the capture edge (at most +1 cycle, and only for the most recent change), so a later change can never overtake an earlier one; or (c) move the random delay to m_vlsit_afifo_sync and apply it to the whole vector, which needs a spec change because the cell is specified as the only home of the model (spec:56, DEC-038). Keep REQ-FUNC-008/009/010 and TEST-008 unchanged. (2) If the designer decides the per-bit model as written is required, the spec must explain how REQ-FUNC-008/009/010 can still hold under it. For example, require each bit's extra delay to be bounded so it is always less than one source update interval, and add that as a stimulus constraint (pointer update rate vs destination period) in contract CHK-015/016/029. (3) Test side: no change to CHK-013. Optionally add an internal coherence monitor that flags when the decoded synchronized pointer is not a value the source pointer recently held. That would confirm the root cause directly in the next run. Do not weaken or disable CHK-013 for model-on runs.

With the per-bit model (cell_sync.sv:158-179), a later bit change can arrive before an earlier delayed one, giving a decoded value above the true pointer (for example 0101→0100→1100 seen as 1101 = 9). The SVA CHK-003 does not fire here, since et<8 and this is not a CHK-003 condition. The failure comes from the TB-only CHK-032 check. It passes in model_off.s1 and syn.s1.
analyses.test_does: verif/tests/test_async_gray_fifo.py:1547-1561: random clock pair (10/37), random ft/et, Traffic, sw_random with 30 sequences (:573-616), final drain. The failing check is in _on_r :269-277. Pre-reset words P are cleared at p_cnt ≥ S+3 read edges after the busy-rise write edge (:269-273, matching contract CHK-005 at :342). Then occ = len(Q)+len(P), and if occ ≤ i_empty_thr, o_empty_thr must be 1. Q only holds writes accepted at write edges before this read edge, so the TB occupancy is an upper bound of what the RTL can legally see (safe direction).

candidates.evidence_for: An RTL estimate larger than the true count needs a synchronized write pointer ahead of the real one. That cannot happen with a coherent Gray crossing, but the spec-mandated per-bit model makes it possible (spec:653 vs :139/:685). A fast write clock against a slow read clock (10/37) makes multi-update reordering likely. The failure occurs only in model-on runs.
candidates.evidence_against: A software reset is in play. A TB P/Q bookkeeping slip around the busy rise or the read release could make the TB occupancy too small, and with no waveform this cannot be fully excluded.

candidates.evidence_for: The read-side CHK-032 check (:274-277) has no software-reset gate, while the write-side one does (:237). P is cleared at a fixed S+3=5 read edges (:271). With the model, the request crossing can take S+2 edges. If P were cleared one edge before the read block shows, the TB occupancy would be too low, and that would look like an optimistic flag.
candidates.evidence_against: While the read side is blocked, rd.sv:118 forces o_empty_thr=1, so an early P clear cannot fail this check during the block. The S+3 clear point is taken from contract CHK-005 (contract.json:342), and the same code passes in model_off.s1 and syn.s1. The same optimistic pattern (RTL estimate on the wrong side) also shows in tests without any software reset (CHK-016, regression).

candidates.evidence_for: The out-of-range synchronized value is produced by the RTL simulation model (cell_sync.sv:146-182). An optimistic estimate on the empty side can also make o_empty=0 too early, which would break REQ-FUNC-009.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows spec 10.6.4 as written, and the datapath and FSMs pass with coherent crossings (syn.s1, model_off.s1).

analyses.options: (1) Spec/model fix as for test_chk_014: a Gray-coherent metastability model, with spec 10.6.4 updated. (2) To rule out the TB bookkeeping candidate, the designer can log len(P), p_cnt and the read-block state at the failing edge. If P was cleared while the read side was not yet blocked, make the P-clear point follow the contract with the model latency (S+2+1), and update contract CHK-005 to match. That is a clarification, not a weakening. (3) Keep the CHK-032 never-optimistic check.
